peopleIntro: Add people and select their existing latitude and longitude states. Add more people with the plus button.
peopleHelp: The unique ID is used in the object tree and should contain lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores. Current coordinates and an OpenStreetMap link are stored for each person.
placesIntro: Add any number of places. The radius determines when a person is considered present at a place.
placesHelp: Only one place can be marked as home. The two fallback values describe the trip from this place to home and are used only if the online route request fails while the person is inside the place radius. Presence and place distances are calculated locally.
routingIntro: Travel-time calculation is optional. At startup, HomeRadar requests one bundled matrix per person for all places. After a successful request, it is refreshed only after a location change of at least 30 meters; after an error, it retries on the next update cycle.
routingHelp: By default, the public OSRM demo service is used without live traffic. If it fails, OpenRouteService can provide a matrix fallback. Create a free account at openrouteservice.org, copy the Basic Key from the API Key tab of the dashboard, and enter it here. The free Standard plan currently allows 500 matrix requests per day and 40 per minute. Each person's matrix is bundled and cached until their location changes by 30 meters.
helpIntro: HomeRadar reads the selected coordinate states and creates per-person states for current location, an OpenStreetMap link, presence, detected places, distances, and travel times.
helpPrivacy: Presence and distances are calculated locally. Travel-time matrices send the person's current coordinates and the configured place coordinates to OSRM; if OSRM fails and the fallback is enabled, they are also sent to OpenRouteService. The OpenStreetMap link is generated locally; the browser is sent to OpenStreetMap with the coordinates only when the link is opened. When a person is within the home radius, travel time home is set to zero locally.
